title: Adapted standard basis at a permissible transform with unchanged degrees
statement:
Let $(T,\mathfrak M,k)$ be a nonzero commutative regular local ring, with residue field $k=T/\mathfrak M$ [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-weil-residue-field]. Fix a regular system of parameters $(x_0,\ldots,x_r,y_1,\ldots,y_s)$, where $r,s\geq0$, and put $P=(x_0,\ldots,x_r)$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. Let $\mathfrak a\subseteq P$ be an ideal, put $R=T/\mathfrak a$, $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak M/\mathfrak a$, $I=P/\mathfrak a$, $A=T/P=R/I$, and assume $G=\operatorname{gr}_I R$ is flat over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring, def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Set $S=G\otimes_A k$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] and $B=k[X_0,\ldots,X_r]$, with all variables of degree one [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-pc-standard-graded-algebra].
Assume $R$ is reduced (it has no nonzero nilpotent elements) and no minimal prime of $R$ contains $I$, where a minimal prime contains no strictly smaller prime. Let $z\in\operatorname{Bl}_I(\operatorname{Spec}R)$ be over $\mathfrak m$ and belong to the chart $\operatorname{Spec}R[I/\bar x_0]$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-nagata-affine-blowup, def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring]. Put
$$D_T=T[t_1,\ldots,t_r]/(x_0t_i-x_i:1\leq i\leq r),\qquad T'=(D_T)_{\mathfrak p'},$$
where $\mathfrak p'$ is the inverse image of $z$ under the surjection $D_T\twoheadrightarrow R[I/\bar x_0]$, $t_i\mapsto\bar x_i/\bar x_0$. Assume $T'$ is regular local, let $R_z=\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Bl}_I(\operatorname{Spec}R),z}$, and put $\mathfrak a'=\ker(T'\twoheadrightarrow R_z)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime].
For a regular local ring $(V,\mathfrak l,\kappa)$ and an ideal $\mathfrak b\subseteq\mathfrak l$, let $E(V,\mathfrak b)=\ker(\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak l}V\to\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak l/\mathfrak b}(V/\mathfrak b))$. Define $\nu^*(V,\mathfrak b)$ to be the nondecreasing sequence containing $d$ with multiplicity $\dim_\kappa(E_d/(\sum_{j=1}^d (\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak l}V)_j E_{d-j}))$, followed by infinitely many $\infty$'s. Equivalently these are the degrees of a minimal homogeneous generating set of $E$, padded by $\infty$.
Let $\mathfrak p\subset k[t_1,\ldots,t_r]$ be the prime of the projective point $z$ in the exceptional ambient fibre chart, whose coordinates are $t_i=X_i/X_0$; it is obtained by reducing the ambient chart modulo $\mathfrak M D_T$. Suppose $\nu^*(T',\mathfrak a')=\nu^*(T,\mathfrak a)$. Then there is a finite sequence $f_1,\ldots,f_m\in\mathfrak a\setminus\{0\}$, possibly empty if $\mathfrak a=0$, with $1\leq d_1\leq\cdots\leq d_m$, such that $f_i\in P^{d_i}$, $f_i\in\mathfrak M^{d_i}\setminus\mathfrak M^{d_i+1}$, and the initial forms $\phi_i=f_i\bmod\mathfrak M^{d_i+1}$ form a minimal homogeneous generating set of $E(T,\mathfrak a)$ in the parameter polynomial ring $\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak M}T=k[X,Y]$. Moreover $\phi_i\in k[X]_{d_i}$ and
$$\phi_i(1,t_1,\ldots,t_r)/1\in\bigl(\mathfrak p\, k[t_1,\ldots,t_r]_{\mathfrak p}\bigr)^{d_i}$$
for every $i$.

source.place: Ancillary source read online: Hironaka, Certain numerical characters of singularities, J. Math. Kyoto Univ. 10 (1970), Proposition 21(i),(ii), p.181, using the order algebra of section 13, p.168, and the chart convention on p.169; the case of equal degree sequences satisfies its non-strict lexicographic hypothesis. The proposition follows from Lemma 20, pp.175–181; https://scispace.com/pdf/certain-numerical-characters-of-singularities-18d51ii5bz.pdf. Archival original WANTED. ILO VIII 2.3.13, p.94, is ancestor motivation only. No Stacks tag states this result.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-normal-flat-double-initial-ideal] with the specified $T,P,\mathfrak a$ and parameters. All its hypotheses occur in the statement: $T$ is regular local, $\mathfrak a\subseteq P$, and $G$ is $A$-flat. Put $C=\ker(B\twoheadrightarrow S)$. The cited statement identifies the parameter polynomial ring with $\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak M}T$ and gives $E(T,\mathfrak a)=Ck[X,Y]$. The degree-zero map $k\to S_0=k$ is the identity, so $C_0=0$.

source.place: Hironaka (1970), Proposition 21, p.181, assembled from Lemma 20 and (19.1); explicit finite induction by Q63.

proof.text: The polynomial ring $B$ is a finitely generated algebra over the field $k$, so [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components] gives that it is Noetherian. Choose finite ideal generators for $C$, and replace each by its finitely many homogeneous components. These components still lie in $C$, since $C$ is a graded kernel, and generate $C$. Remove redundant elements to get a minimal homogeneous generating family $\phi_1,\ldots,\phi_m$, ordered by degrees $d_i\geq1$. Its images form a basis of $C/B_+C$: they span by generation, and a homogeneous linear dependence of their residues in a fixed degree would express one generator as a combination of the other same-degree generators and of lower-degree generators, contradicting minimality. Conversely, generation follows by induction on degree from spanning this quotient: subtract constant combinations in degree $d$, then write the remainder in $\sum_{j>0}B_jC_{d-j}$ and apply the smaller-degree cases. This also explains the degree multiplicities in $\nu^*$.

source.place: Tag 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence), as specialized by the cited finite-type-field leaf; elementary homogeneous-component and degree-induction arguments.

proof.text: The same $\phi_i$ form a minimal homogeneous generating set of $Ck[X,Y]$: generation follows by expanding coefficients in $Y$, and a relation making one generator redundant would, on setting $Y=0$, make it redundant in $C$. Thus $(d_1,\ldots,d_m,\infty,\ldots)=\nu^*(T,\mathfrak a)$. If $m=0$, Step 1 gives $E=0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-krull-intersection-jacobson], $\bigcap_n\mathfrak M^nT=0$: $T$ is Noetherian local, $\mathfrak M$ is its Jacobson radical, and $T$ is generated by $1$ as a module over itself. A nonzero $f\in\mathfrak a$ would therefore have finite $\mathfrak M$-order and a nonzero initial form in $E$, a contradiction. Hence $m=0$ implies $\mathfrak a=0$; the empty family proves the assertion in that case. Continue with $m\geq1$.

source.place: Tag 00IQ (lemma-intersection-powers-ideal-module), part (2); elementary polynomial retraction and finite-order argument.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence], the full parameter list is regular. Its $x$-prefix is regular directly from [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]: its successive multiplication conditions are a prefix of those of the full list, and its final quotient is nonzero because $P\subseteq\mathfrak M$. Apply [lem-pur-regular-sequence-graded-polynomial] to that prefix. It identifies $\operatorname{gr}_PT=A[X]$, sending $X_i$ to $[x_i]_1$, with its displayed monomial formula. In degree $d$ let $K_d$ be the kernel of $A[X]_d\twoheadrightarrow G_d$. This map is onto: every class in $I^d/I^{d+1}$ is a sum of degree-$d$ products of the generators $\bar x_i$ with coefficients reduced to $A$.

Each $G_d$ is an $A$-direct summand of $G=\bigoplus_eG_e$, hence flat by [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]: tensor an injection with the split inclusion $G_d\to G$; the tensor projection splits that inclusion, so injectivity for the full $G$ implies injectivity for $G_d$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-quotient-tensor-injective] to $0\to K_d\to A[X]_d\to G_d\to0$ and the left tensor factor $k$. It gives $\ker(k\otimes_A A[X]_d\to k\otimes_AG_d)=\operatorname{im}(k\otimes_AK_d)$. Explicitly $\lambda\otimes\sum a_\alpha X^\alpha\mapsto\sum\lambda\bar a_\alpha X^\alpha$ identifies the middle term with $B_d$, and tensor swapping identifies the last term with $S_d$. The resulting map is precisely $\beta_d$. Therefore every $\phi\in C_d$ is a finite sum $\sum_\ell\lambda_\ell\bar u_\ell$ with $u_\ell\in K_d$. Lift each $\lambda_\ell\in k$ to $a_\ell\in A$; then $u=\sum_\ell a_\ell u_\ell\in K_d$ reduces to $\phi$.

source.place: Tag 00HL (lemma-flat-tor-zero); degreewise application and explicit monomial tensor identification.

proof.text: For each $\phi_i$, choose $u_i=\sum_{|\alpha|=d_i}a_\alpha X^\alpha\in K_{d_i}$ reducing to $\phi_i$. Lift its coefficients to $T$ and put $b_i=\sum\widetilde a_\alpha x^\alpha\in P^{d_i}$. Since $u_i\in K_{d_i}$, the image of $b_i$ in $R$ lies in $I^{d_i+1}$. The map $P^{d_i+1}\to I^{d_i+1}$ is onto by the definition $I=P/\mathfrak a$; choose $e_i\in P^{d_i+1}$ with that image and set $f_i=b_i-e_i$. Then $f_i\in\mathfrak a\cap P^{d_i}$, and its class modulo $\mathfrak M^{d_i+1}$ is $\phi_i$: $e_i$ vanishes there, and each coefficient may be reduced modulo $\mathfrak M$. In particular $f_i$ is nonzero of order exactly $d_i$. These $f_i$ give the initial standard basis to which the correction will be applied.

source.place: Hironaka (1970), (19.1), p.176; representative calculation from the preceding exact sequence, written out by Q63.

proof.text: Use [lem-trf-parameter-blowup-algebra-regular] with the full parameter list, subset $\{x_0,\ldots,x_r\}$ and distinguished parameter $x_0$. This subset is nonempty and the dimension is $r+s+1\geq1$. It identifies $D_T[1/x_0]=T[1/x_0]$ and makes multiplication by $x_0$ on $D_T$ injective, so $D_T$ embeds in that localization. If $f\in P^d$, write $f=\sum_{|\alpha|=d}a_\alpha x^\alpha$. Its quotient by $x_0^d$ is $\sum a_\alpha t_1^{\alpha_1}\cdots t_r^{\alpha_r}\in D_T$, with $x_0/x_0=1$. Thus each $g_i=f_i/x_0^{d_i}$ is a well-defined element of $T'$. Put $H=(x_0,y_1,\ldots,y_s)T'$, and define $U_d=\{\phi\in B_d:\phi(1,t)/1\in(\mathfrak p k[t]_{\mathfrak p})^d\}$.

source.place: Hironaka (1970), (13.1), p.168, chart convention p.169 and (19.1)–(19.2), p.176; ambient chart facts as in the cited parameter-blowup lemma.

proof.text: Induct on $a=1,\ldots,m+1$. The invariant before stage $a$ is: the current $f_i$ lie in $\mathfrak a\cap P^{d_i}$, have orders $d_i$, and have minimal homogeneous initial forms generating $E$; and, for each $j<a$, $\phi_j\in U_{d_j}$ and there is $w_j\in H(g_1,\ldots,g_{j-1})T'$ with $\operatorname{ord}_{\mathfrak M'}(g_j-w_j)=d_j$. At $a=1$ the latter requirements are empty and Steps 3–7 establish the former. The numerical hypothesis gives $\nu^*(T',\mathfrak a')_j=d_j$ for every $j\leq m$, throughout the induction: the ring and ideal defining this sequence never change, and the list of degrees of the current basis will be preserved.

source.place: Hironaka (1970), Proposition 21, p.181, assembled from Lemma 20 and (19.1); explicit finite induction by Q63.

proof.text: At stage $a\leq m$, apply [lem-trf-permissible-standard-basis-one-step] to the current full list. Its ambient rings, chart point, reducedness, absence of components in the center, and flatness are exactly those assumed here. The earlier-index hypotheses are the induction invariant and numerical equality; the remaining hypothesis is $\nu^*(T',\mathfrak a')_a=d_a\geq d_a$. Obtain $c_j\in P^{d_a-d_j}$ and $v_a\in H(g_1,\ldots,g_{a-1})T'$ such that $f_a^*=f_a-\sum_{j<a}c_jf_j$ has order $d_a$, initial form in $U_{d_a}$, and its divided transform $g_a^*$ satisfies $\operatorname{ord}_{\mathfrak M'}(g_a^*-v_a)=d_a$. Replace only $f_a$ by $f_a^*$ and take $w_a=v_a$.

source.place: Hironaka (1970), Proposition 21, p.181, assembled from Lemma 20 and (19.1); explicit finite induction by Q63.

proof.text: Check preservation of the invariant explicitly. Each $c_jf_j$ lies in $P^{d_a-d_j}P^{d_j}=P^{d_a}$ and in $\mathfrak a$, so $f_a^*\in\mathfrak a\cap P^{d_a}$. In degree $d_a$ its initial form is $\phi_a^*=\phi_a-\sum_{j<a}\bar c_j\phi_j$, where $\bar c_j$ denotes the degree-$(d_a-d_j)$ class of $c_j$ in $\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak M}T$ (possibly zero). This elementary triangular generator replacement is invertible, using $\phi_a=\phi_a^*+\sum\bar c_j\phi_j$. It preserves generation of $E$ and minimality: on $E/(k[X,Y]_+E)$ it subtracts only constant combinations of earlier generators of the same degree, an invertible triangular change of basis. The new form belongs to $k[X]$ because it belongs to $U_{d_a}$. Earlier $f_j,g_j,w_j$ are unchanged; their correction conditions use only indices smaller than $j$, so they persist. All later $f_i$ are unchanged. This proves the invariant at $a+1$.

source.place: Hironaka (1970), Proposition 21, p.181, assembled from Lemma 20 and (19.1); explicit finite induction by Q63.

proof.text: At $a=m+1$ the induction has corrected every index. Retain the resulting $f_1,\ldots,f_m$ and discard the auxiliary $g_i,w_i$. They lie in $\mathfrak a\setminus\{0\}$, have the prescribed $P$- and $\mathfrak M$-orders, and their initial forms minimally generate $E$. For each $i$, membership $\phi_i\in U_{d_i}$ says, by its displayed definition, exactly that $\phi_i\in k[X]_{d_i}$ and $\phi_i(1,t)/1\in(\mathfrak p k[t]_{\mathfrak p})^{d_i}$. These are all conclusions of the item. The case $\mathfrak a=0$ was already handled in Step 3.

source.place: Hironaka (1970), Proposition 21, p.181, assembled from Lemma 20 and (19.1); explicit finite induction by Q63.
